AI code review results below, please doublecheck

Looks good - the entry accounting, the head/middle/tail split and the copy loop all hold up, and the pool order used is bounded by CDP_EXT_MAX_PAGES so the transient cl_page cp_npgs/cp_len fields still fit. COMMIT_MSG (the m4 hunk): the message now describes it and says why it
is an independent build fix -- copy_folio_to_iter() arrived in v5.19
and __filemap_get_folio() in v5.16, so kernels in between did not
build.  Added

    Fixes: 59d84ec3ffb8 ("LU-19249 build: Compatibility updates for kernel v6.16")

Keeping it in this patch rather than splitting it out: the same probe
is what gates LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER here, so a separate change would
have to land first for this one to be correct.

cl_io.c:1938 (read clamp): right, it is dead, and for exactly the
reason given.  Removed it and LL_DIO_READ_COPY_SPANS with it.

Taking that rather than the other option -- dropping the
HAVE_COPY_FOLIO_TO_ITER term from LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER -- because
that term is deliberate.  Without copy_folio_to_iter(), a multi-page
entry has to be read back a page at a time, and each pass flushes the
whole folio, so the flushing cost grows with the square of the entry
size.  Order 0 on 5.16-5.18 is the cheaper of the two.  The comment on
LL_DIO_POOL_MAX_ORDER already records this, so the coupling is not
lost with the macro.

cl_io.c:1596 (unit check robot): the flagged expression, npages -
head, no longer exists; the count is now built up in a local.

Patch Set 15:

sanity test_56ab ("lfs find --blocks") on patch set 15, session
1209a807-ec16-42ff-ba05-e57bae494378, is a race in the test on ZFS,
not this patch.

The test writes 8 KiB at 16 MiB, 4 KiB at 16 MiB and 2 MiB at 16 MiB
into three files and expects exactly one of them to report more than
1 MiB of blocks.  On a ZFS OST the two sparse files are not cheap: the
object is far larger than one record, so a single small write in the
middle allocates a full record.  The test only passes while that
allocation has not been reported back to the client.

ls -ls in the failing run:
     2  f56ab.sanity.1
  1028  f56ab.sanity.2
  2052  f56ab.sanity.3

ls -ls in a passing el9.8 review-dne-zfs-part-1 run the same day
(session 79b5dd6c-1eb0-42f0-8d8c-dde921fd4791):
     2  f56ab.sanity.1
     2  f56ab.sanity.2
  2052  f56ab.sanity.3

4 KiB write was charged a full 1 MiB record.  The only difference
between the runs is whether the OST had reported that yet.  The test
does sync_all_data and then wait_zfs_commit ost1 2, which waits on
ost1 alone while the three files are on different OSTs.

Nothing in this series is in that path.  The writes are buffered dd,
page cache large folios are off on el9.x (no
mapping_set_folio_order_range), and the block count comes from record
allocation on the OST.  68619 in this same series, one patch down,
ran the same subtest in the same test group on the same distro
(session 040fc480-e88b-4d55-a541-ad0e6852b4fe) and passed it.

have been fixed, but got: 4", is the same class of failure I described
on 68619 for 18b/18c, and is not from this series.

The lfsck orphan counters are filesystem-global and sanity-lfsck does
not clean up between subtests -- check_mount_and_prep only removes the
current $tdir -- so OST-objects left unreferenced by an earlier
subtest are counted.  18e runs a full repair (lfsck_start -r -o -c)
after 18a through 18d have each left their directories behind, and it
overcounted by exactly 2.

runs and distros, which a defect in orphan accounting would not do.

commit.message:
LU-19895 clio: use large folios for unaligned DIO

The unaligned DIO bounce buffer was filled from the order 0
pool, one page and one cl_page per PAGE_SIZE, so it never
benefited from the multi-order folio extents the aligned path
now builds.  It matters more than the aligned case in practice:
the client allocates this buffer itself, so no THP backed user
buffer is needed, and hybrid IO routes ordinary buffered writes
into exactly this path.

Fill the buffer from the compound page pools: the bulk from the
largest order which fits (within one brw_ext), the remainder
from order 0.  Per-chunk bookkeeping falls from one
cl_page/oap/brw_ext per PAGE_SIZE to one per folio extent -
16384 entries to ~320 for a 64MiB chunk.  The high order is
tried once; a binary decomposition would reach ~73 entries but
costs an all-or-nothing contiguous allocation per order, on
pools this node may otherwise never use.

ll_free_dio_buffer() follows the piecewise fill: it walks the
array in runs of a common order, takes that order from cdp_npgs
rather than folio_order(), stops at the first NULL so a partly
filled array is never handed back to the pool, and clears
cdp_page_count.

A zero length request fails with -EINVAL rather than building an
empty cdp.  Encrypted files keep order 0 entries
(cdp_no_coalesce).

The copy loop is reworked with the entries.  A write flushes
the dcache once per entry rather than once per copy; a short
write copy re-faults the user pages and retries; the
short_copies budget resets each pass, so it bounds a pass
rather than the whole sub-DIO; the refault covers what the next
pass will ask for, since asking for only what this one had left
lets the retry come up short again and spend the budget while
making progress; and a single write copy is
bounded because it runs under kmap_atomic() with pagefaults
disabled -- at 64KiB where copy_folio_from_iter_atomic()
exists and highmem is off, at the page boundary otherwise.

The entry order is clamped to cdp_max_ext_pgs as well, so a
buffer entry cannot exceed the target's pages-per-RPC any more
than a user buffer entry can.

sanity 119v covers the dio_large_folios gate, which needs this
buffer to observe, and 119w checks the pages-per-RPC clamp from
this side: with max_pages_per_rpc tuned to half of
CDP_EXT_MAX_PAGES, an unaligned DIO must not put a wider bucket
in rpc_stats.
